_README: Canonical input registry. New tools SHOULD reuse these input `id`s and constraints verbatim. Two tools that share an id collapse into a single column in the /pro batch grid; if they also share type + constraints (number min/max/step, select options, color palette), that column becomes bulk-writable - one value fills every row. The catalog validator (scripts/validate-catalog.ts) emits a WARNING (never an error) when a tool uses one of these ids with a divergent type or constraints, so drift is visible without blocking. Labels here are advisory: a tool may show its own label (the /pro header uses the first non-empty one). Adding a new shared input? Add it here first, then adopt it. This is deliberately data, not docs - the authoring guide will link here.

body.label: Body
body.description: Main body copy (markdown where the tool renders it).

windowStyle.label: Window buttons
windowStyle.description: Window-manager chrome look for a framed window: Nuremberg = GNOME Adwaita, Cupertino = macOS, Redmond = Windows. Shared by snippet and frame (plans/147).

eventName.label: Event name
eventName.description: Name of the event (badge, calendar payload, signage).

eventStart.label: Starts
eventStart.description: Event start. Shipped as a URL contract by qr-code's calendar payload (plans/147 E1).

eventLocation.label: Location
eventLocation.description: Where the event happens (a room, venue or address as one line).

awardtopic.label: Course or award
awardtopic.description: What a certificate or badge is for - a course title, award name or contribution. Roster tools share it so one CSV column feeds them all (plans/147 T8; ratified 2026-08-25).

awarddate.label: Award date
awarddate.description: The date shown on a certificate or award. Shared with roster tools so one CSV column feeds them all (plans/147 T8; ratified 2026-08-25).

sourceAuthor.label: Author
sourceAuthor.description: Author or creator credited as the source. Shared by deck-studio and doc-studio (plans/147 M1 id audit; ratified 2026-08-25).

imageFraming.label: Zoom & Position
imageFraming.description: The whole envelope of an image inside its frame: zoom + pan (object-position with a scale), roll, and the two perspective axes. THE framing control - pair it with `framingFor: "<assetInputId>"` so the shell mounts its generic on-canvas overlay and offers 'Use as a new image'. Every field is opt-in: a tool that only pans declares x/y, one that straightens adds `rotate`, one that corrects converging verticals adds `pitch`/`yaw` (the Geometry panel in Lightroom, 'Adjust' in Instagram). Render it with the {{framing}} helper - never a hand-written object-position string - so the canvas, every export path and the hooks' frameRect()/drawFramed() place the image identically. Note pitch/yaw make the placement a projective homography, which SVG and PDF cannot express: those exports take the walker's posed-raster path for that element. See plans/148.

imageFit.label: Fit
imageFit.description: How the image fills its frame before framing is applied: cover crops to fill, contain letterboxes. The companion select to `imageFraming` (vector fields are numbers, so fit cannot live inside it). Declare it with `attachTo: "<assetInputId>"` and `display: "icon-toggle"` so it rides on the asset row as one button rather than taking a row of its own.

imageCrop.label: Crop
imageCrop.description: An explicit crop RECTANGLE in percent of the source image. Only for the case where the crop sets the OUTPUT size (screencap): everywhere the frame is fixed, the crop is derived from imageFraming's zoom + pan and this input should not exist. Two canonical ids, deliberately, because they answer different questions.

conventions.typography: Per-element typography numbers use `<element>FontSize` and `<element>FontWeight` (e.g. headingFontSize, bodyFontWeight). Weight is a number with min 100, max 900, step 100. Size is a relative number whose range the tool defines.
conventions.bulkWrite: A /pro column is bulk-writable only when every tool that declares the id agrees on type AND constraints - number min/max/step, select option values, color palette, and a vector's per-field min/max/step. Match the values above to keep the column actionable.
conventions.imageFraming: One image slot takes at most three ids: the `asset` input itself, its `imageFraming` vector (framingFor: the asset's id), and an `imageFit` select attached to the asset row. Prefix all three together for a second slot on the same tool (bgImage + bgFraming + bgFit); inside a `blocks` row, where there is no vector sub-field type, the same values live as sibling numbers <base>Zoom / <base>X / <base>Y / <base>Rotate / <base>Pitch / <base>Yaw and the {{framing}} helper's block mode reads them. Never invent a fourth spelling.
